skills.trigger: When evaluating a large thoracic mass on chest X-ray to determine local invasion versus displacement.
steps: Inspect the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm contour and position; a normal, smooth dome shape below the mass indicates the phrenic nerve is intact, whereas elevation or paralysis suggests nerve invasion.

Examine the mediastinal border and adjacent vascular structures for sharp, preserved fat planes or distinct margins, which indicate the mass is pushing structures aside (displacement) rather than infiltrating them.
Assess the internal texture of the mass; homogeneous opacity supports a benign or contained process, while heterogeneity might suggest necrosis or complex malignancy.

skills.trigger: When characterizing the morphology and boundaries of a pulmonary or mediastinal opacity.
steps: Trace the perimeter of the opacity to determine if margins are well-circumscribed (sharp, defined) or ill-defined (fuzzy, spiculated).
Evaluate the density uniformity across the lesion to classify it as homogenous (uniform whiteness) or heterogeneous (mixed densities).
Correlate the mass location with adjacent anatomical landmarks (e.g., diaphragm, heart border, vessels) to confirm if interfaces are maintained or obliterated.
